title: The best revenge
hook: the best revenge is not to become like the one who wronged you (Meditations 6.6)

segments.voice: Yesterday: cold or warm, the duty that doesn't wait for perfect conditions. Your line was nobody claps, the work is good anyway. And today the week closes.

Someone cuts you off in traffic, then honks at you. A coworker takes credit in the meeting. A relative says the cutting thing at dinner, the one they always say. And instantly, the reply is ready: sharper, faster, a little crueler, because they started it. It can feel like justice. Marcus Aurelius was an emperor. He could have answered almost any insult with real force. In book six he writes himself one short sentence about revenge.
screen: `THE REPLY IS ALREADY LOADED.` → `AN EMPEROR'S OPTIONS.` → `ONE SENTENCE ON REVENGE.`

segments.voice: Meditations six, six, in George Long's translation: "The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like the wrong doer." He doesn't say there's no such thing as being wronged. Someone did wrong. The question is what you do next. When someone is rude and you're rude back, two people have now been rude, and one of them is you. Their behavior has reached inside you and rearranged you. For a Stoic, that's the only real damage they could do. Your money, your reputation, those are outside. Your character is the one thing that's yours, and mirroring them hands it over. Why call it revenge? Marcus could have said forgive, or rise above it. Instead he keeps the word revenge, and there's something a little sly in that. He lets the hurt part of you have its wish to win, then changes what winning means. The wrongdoer wanted you smaller. You stay the size you were. Now look back at this week. How am I using my soul. Heraclitus. Bad breath, where someone's mouth is just their mouth. Soon ashes, and meanwhile, do good. The child's top. Cold or warm. And now this. Nearly every one of those lines is about the same small room: the space between what happens to you and what you become because of it. Marcus keeps returning to that room, because it's the one place nobody else can enter without your permission.
screen: `AVENGE YOURSELF: DON'T BECOME THEM.` · `MIRRORING HANDS THEM YOUR CHARACTER.` · `HE KEEPS THE WORD REVENGE.` · `THIS WEEK: THE SAME SMALL ROOM.` · then, large: `NOT LIKE THEM.`

segments.voice: Recall one recent moment when someone was rude or unfair to you, and notice where the comeback sits in your body: jaw, chest, hands. Now replay the scene with you answering in your own voice instead of theirs, calm, plain, maybe silent. Not weak; just not like them.
George Long, whose translation gives Marcus's line: the best way of avenging yourself is not to become like the one who wronged you. Today's word.
Your line: not like them. You stay the size you were. Week's end; see you tomorrow.

howItsDone: People who draw on Marcus often repeat 'not like them' when someone is rude, as a reminder to answer in their own manner rather than mirroring the other person's.

fork.setup: a coworker takes credit for your work in a meeting. what's the best revenge, by Marcus's line?
options: take credit for theirs next week.
say the true thing plainly, in your own manner, without copying theirs.
fork.reveal: Meditations 6.6: the best way of avenging yourself is not to become like the wrongdoer. Speaking up isn't ruled out; mirroring is.

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice way of saying let it go.
what it means: you were wronged, and the real loss would be letting the wrong reshape your character.
what a scholar hears: Stoics held that only your own choices can harm you, so mirroring the wrongdoer is the one injury the wrongdoer can't do to you without your help.
recall: belonging that widens to all people

chat.says: My roommate was rude to me, so I was rude back. Fair is fair, right?
options: The best revenge is not becoming like them; now two people were rude.
Yes, matching their rudeness is the only way they'll ever learn.
No, you should pretend nothing wrong happened and say nothing ever.
